title: Service-to-Egress Matrix and Firewall Consolidation Plan
content:
Summary:
This is a working plan for consolidating service-level egress rules and firewall policies across our VPC/on-prem private deployments. Goal is to reduce rule count, standardize service-to-egress mappings, and provide a safe Terraform-driven upgrade path with automated test gates and rollback. This doc mixes a matrix (service -> egress pattern), Terraform module interface notes, staged rollout steps, and test/rollback scenarios.

Context & motivation:
- Current state: many clusters and on-prem sites have ad-hoc NATs, scattered firewall rules, and duplicate allowlists. Hard to reason about cross-site connectivity and private DNS resolution for downstream SaaS endpoints.
- Problems seen: tokenized IP whitelists that break during egress scaling, slow incident resolution because firewall owners differ by cluster, and rule drift after manual hotfixes.
- Non-goal: this doc does not attempt to invent a service mesh or change application-level TLS strategies. Focus is network policy, egress, and the infra-side controls.

Scope:
- In-scope: service classification, canonical egress patterns (internet, partner-saas, internal-only), stub/private DNS handling, NAT topology choices (centralized vs localized), firewall rule consolidation, and Terraform module interfaces for policy rollout.
- Out-of-scope: app code changes, SSO identity changes, or long-term audit policy retention beyond 90d.

Service-to-egress matrix (working):
Columns: service_name | consumers | desired_egress_class | preferred_nat_style | dns_resolution_hint | break_glass_policy
- model-fetcher | inference, batch-workers | partner-saas (model-hub.api.com) | localized NAT + egress cache | private-dns override -> model-hub.internal | allow-direct (ops-owned)
- telemetry-relay | observability backend | internet (outbound TLS to *.observability.com) | centralized NAT (shared egress pool) | use public DNS with EDNS | redirect-to-proxy if rate-limited
- feature-flagger | product / clients | internal-only (control plane) | no-nat (internal route) | internal SRV records | emergency-only egress via canary gateway
- data-exporter | external-data-lakes | partner-saas (SFTP) | centralized NAT + static egress IP | split-horizon: export endpoints on stub DNS | manual approval ticket required

Notes on classification: keep classes coarse to avoid explosion of firewall rules. Map many services to 3 canonical classes: internal, partner-saas, internet.

Firewall consolidation strategy (high level):
1) Introduce intent-layer: translate service-to-egress matrix into canonical allowlists per egress-class instead of per-service rules.
2) Combine overlaps: where multiple services share identical egress endpoints, publish a single firewall object (egress-group).
3) Prefer tag-based rules (k8s labels or cloud tags) referencing 'egress-class' instead of explicit host lists.
4) Keep a thin mapping layer for exceptions (break_glass_policy).
5) Build automated tests to verify equivalence: for each service, synthetic requests should succeed against old rules and new consolidated rules in staging.

Terraform module notes (interface & behavior):
Module name: redwood/private-egress-policy
- Variables (working list): env (string), cluster_id (string), services (list of objects but in practice we accept list of ids), egress_groups (map of cidr/host lists), nat_mode (enum: centralized|localized|none), stub_dns_zones (map), static_egress_ips (list), policy_version (string)
- Outputs: applied_policy_id, change_plan_summary, test_endpoints (list)
- Semantics: module must produce a planable set of firewall rules (cloud provider firewall or on-prem ACL entries) + manifest (YAML) per cluster for SRE review.
- Migration helpers: a 'preflight' mode that only generates change_plan_summary and a 'dry-run' that applies to a shadow namespace to validate kube-networkpolicy changes.
- Backwards-compat: when nat_mode changes, module emits no destructive change to existing NAT gateways until a flag confirm_migration is true.

Staged rollout (recommended):
A. Prep (validate & catalog)
- Inventory: run discovery script to map existing egress rules and active flows (example script: scripts/discover-egress.py).
- Author canonical matrix; review with owners.
- Add minimal tagging on services: egress-class tag.
B. Staging (shadow testing)
- Apply module in preflight mode in staging clusters.
- Deploy synthetic test pods that exercise each service's downstream endpoints.
- Compare flow logs (before vs after) for 48 hours.
C. Canary (single region/non-critical cluster)
- Deploy consolidated rules behind a canary toggle.
- Run 24–72h smoke tests + load tests for connection churn scenarios.
D. Gradual roll (multiple clusters)
- Batch clusters by risk profile: dev -> qa -> prod-noncritical -> prod-critical.
- For each batch: apply with confirm_migration=false (dry-run), then a short maintenance window to set confirm_migration=true.

Testing & validation checklist:
- TCP/UDP connectivity to expected endpoints
- DNS resolution paths: ensure private stub returns partner IPs in on-prem zones
- Egress IP verification: outbound probes to ipinfo-style service to assert static IPs
- Latency/regression check for requests routed via centralized NAT/proxy
- Log/Alert smoke: no new 5xx in downstream services for 2 windows

Rollback plan:
- All Terraform applies include a tagged backup state snapshot and a change-plan id.
- If regression detected within 2h window: revert confirm_migration flag and re-apply previous policy (fast path).
- For DNS-related regressions: revert stub DNS zone changes first before firewall rules.

Monitoring & post-mortem metrics:
- Flow log delta per service (blocked vs allowed)
- Authenticated session drop rate for inference paths
- Number of manual exceptions created (should trend down)
- Time-to-restore for rollback operations

Open questions / risks:
- Split-horizon DNS TTLs across on-prem caches may delay rollback effectiveness. Need TTL hygiene and cache flush procedures.
- Centralized NAT is simpler to reason about but increases blast radius; localized NAT reduces surface but complicates static-IP requirements.
- Regulatory sites that require per-customer egress isolation will need an exception pattern.

Next actions (short):
- Ravi: run discovery script and publish raw mapping (due 2025-10-07).
- Linus: prototype the module preflight mode and share example plan (due 2025-10-14).
- Maya: schedule matrix review with product infra and security (calendar invite + Confluence notes)

Appendix: quick commands
- discovery: python scripts/discover-egress.py --cluster all --output csv
- preflight: terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -target=module.private_egress -out=plan.tfplan
- dry-apply (shadow): terraform apply -var confirm_mode=shadow plan.tfplan

End of draft.

Feedback wanted: are the classes coarse enough? any compliance constraints we missed for specific regions? any objection to conservative confirm_migration gating?
